pharm: Binds intracellular estrogen receptors to regulate gene transcription, replacing endogenous estrogen and supporting estrogen-responsive tissues.
quick: Vasomotor/atrophy: 1-2 mg once daily, lowest effective dose
May be taken with or without food
Use with caution; no specific adjustment
May raise circulating estradiol levels acutely
summary: Oral estradiol is used as menopausal hormone therapy for moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms and vulvar/vaginal atrophy, for hypoestrogenism, and for osteoporosis prevention, and as palliative therapy in certain breast and prostate cancers. It carries a boxed warning for endometrial cancer (unopposed estrogen), and for cardiovascular events, stroke, venous thromboembolism, and probable dementia. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration, and add a progestin in women with an intact uterus.
indications: Moderate-to-severe symptoms of vulvar and vaginal atrophy of menopause
Hypoestrogenism due to hypogonadism, castration, or primary ovarian failure
Palliative treatment of metastatic breast cancer in appropriately selected patients
Palliative treatment of advanced androgen-dependent prostate cancer

dosage.d: Start 1 mg once daily; titrate to lowest effective dose (typically 1-2 mg/day)
0.5 mg once daily cyclically (e.g., 23 days on, 5 days off), lowest effective dose
1-2 mg once daily, adjusted to response
10 mg three times daily for at least 3 months
Add a progestin to estrogen therapy

admin: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals
Add a progestin in women with an intact uterus to reduce endometrial cancer risk; a woman without a uterus does not need a progestin
Reevaluate periodically (e.g., every 3-6 months) for continued need
Investigate any undiagnosed persistent or recurring abnormal vaginal bleeding (endometrial sampling)
Discontinue at least 4-6 weeks before surgery with high thromboembolic risk or prolonged immobilization, if feasible
moa: Estradiol is the principal endogenous estrogen. It diffuses into target cells and binds nuclear estrogen receptors, forming a complex that modulates transcription of estrogen-responsive genes. This restores estrogenic effects on the hypothalamus/pituitary (suppressing FSH/LH), genitourinary tract, bone (reducing resorption), and vasomotor regulation, relieving menopausal symptoms and preserving bone mass.

absolute: Known, suspected, or history of breast cancer (except selected palliative use)
Active or recent (within ~1 year) arterial thromboembolic disease (stroke, MI)
Active deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or history of these
Known protein C, protein S, or antithrombin deficiency / thrombophilic disorders

preg: Estradiol is contraindicated in pregnancy; there is no indication for use during pregnancy. Discontinue if pregnancy occurs.
lact: Estrogens are present in breast milk and can reduce the quantity and quality of milk; avoid during breastfeeding or use with caution.
renal: Use with caution; fluid retention may worsen conditions affected by renal status. No specific dose adjustment is established.
hepatic: Contraindicated in liver dysfunction or disease; estrogens are extensively hepatically metabolized and may be poorly metabolized and accumulate, and can worsen cholestasis.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St. John's wort) - reduce estradiol levels and efficacy
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) - increase estradiol exposure and adverse effects
moderate: Thyroid hormone (estrogen increases binding globulin; may raise levothyroxine requirement)
Anticoagulants (estrogen is procoagulant; may oppose anticoagulant effect)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Acute alcohol intake may transiently increase circulating estradiol.
interactions.diagnostics: Increases thyroid-binding globulin, sex hormone-binding globulin, and various coagulation factors; can alter related laboratory tests.

monitoring: Annual breast exam and mammography per guidelines
Lipids and glucose in at-risk patients
counsel: Report any unusual vaginal bleeding promptly
Seek urgent care for chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, leg swelling/pain, severe headache, vision loss, or weakness on one side
Do calf/breast self-checks and keep up with mammograms
Tell your doctor if you smoke - it greatly increases clot and stroke risk
Use the lowest dose for the shortest time needed and attend regular reviews
pk: Symptom relief over days to weeks
Plasma Tmax ~ several hours after oral dosing
Estradiol ~ short; metabolites recirculate (effective half-life longer)
Store at 20-25 C; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Boxed warning: endometrial cancer with unopposed estrogen, plus cardiovascular, stroke, VTE, and probable dementia risks
Always add a progestin if the uterus is intact; not needed after hysterectomy
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration and reassess regularly
Contraindicated in liver disease and active/prior thromboembolism
Smoking sharply increases cardiovascular and thromboembolic risk
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume your schedule. Do not double up. Missed doses may cause breakthrough bleeding.
overdose: Overdose may cause nausea, vomiting, breast tenderness, fluid retention, and withdrawal bleeding in women. There is no specific antidote; manage supportively.
